inspection_scope: Rough visual review of all eight shots in captioned and captionless 360×640 evidence, including every supplied consecutive contact/impact/handoff/landing window. Assessed silhouette, canonical acting, materials, hierarchy, composition, mobile meaning, contacts, local reactions, energy, irregularity and event accents.

gates.evidence: Participating Bot poses clearly progress through focused, burdened, surprised, worried and relieved states. Head angle, face, antennae and body compression remain readable at native mobile size; absent-Bot shots are treated separately.

Object-to-object mechanisms generally retain visible links, but several declared Bot contacts are not painted as contacts: the lifted roof is remote from Bot’s hand in shot 01, the checkpoint control is weakly connected in shot 03, both rain pulls lack a hand-to-anchor connection, the rollback hands do not occupy the two tab grips, and the finale lever press is not visible.

Active beats develop through clear state changes, bounded reactions and useful recognition holds. The comparison hold, dry-test inspection and final restored-house hold serve the story rather than reading as arbitrary dead caption holds.
The rowhouse has a distinctive asymmetric paper silhouette, coherent teal/coral/gold material coding, visible layered edges and designed irregularity consistent across both caption modes.

Most shots stage the house and mechanisms intentionally, but the checkpoint hero in shot 03 is visually submerged by the house/Bot, and shot 08’s large generic yellow bays overlap and dominate the live house instead of reading as subordinate flanking archive states.

The roof exchange, leak and restoration survive without captions, but the checkpoint capture in shot 03 and the checkpoint-versus-failed archive states in shot 08 are not independently legible at 360×640.

violations.observation: At the declared roof contact and throughout the loaded lift, the teal roof travels far above Bot while Bot’s right hand remains near the body/window area; no hand-to-eave attachment is visible.
violations.smallest_correction: Seat the right hand visibly on the teal eave at frame 50 and keep that inverse grip attached through frame 175, including the burdened hold.

violations.observation: The checkpoint-control pull is not visibly transmitted from Bot’s hand to a distinct tab; the hand, small control and surrounding house layers merge at mobile size.
violations.smallest_correction: Bring the checkpoint tab in front of Bot, place the right hand directly on its grip, and maintain that attachment through the archive pull.

violations.observation: At the capture impact, the house remains the dominant silhouette while the intended plate, pressure cam, relief registration and dry cassette are reduced to small marks; the sentence’s checkpoint hero has no clear focal hierarchy.
violations.smallest_correction: Expose one broad gold plate edge and one enlarged cam/cassette registration area in front of or clearly beside the house during frames 278–298.

violations.observation: Without captions, the native frames read as Bot standing beside an intact house with decorative gold markers, not as a dry house state being physically captured and locked.
violations.smallest_correction: Enlarge the plate stamp and dry-floor cassette into a single high-contrast before-to-locked state that remains unobscured at 360×640.

violations.observation: The water path is readable, but the declared Bot-driven rain pull is not: the top ribbon anchor is remote from Bot and no visible tether or continuous hand attachment connects the pull to the reservoir release.
violations.smallest_correction: Extend a visible ribbon/tether from Bot’s gripping hand to the reservoir anchor and keep it taut through the measured pull.

violations.observation: At the two-grip rollback contact, Bot’s hands remain clustered at the chest rather than occupying distinct left and right tab anchors; the later carriage motion therefore appears mechanically self-driven.
violations.smallest_correction: Separate both arms, seat each hand on its named tab grip, and preserve both attachments until the carriage locks.

violations.observation: The repeated test again lacks a visible Bot-hand connection to the rain anchor, despite the water itself following a clear roof-to-gutter path.
violations.smallest_correction: Reuse the corrected visible hand-to-ribbon tether from shot 05 for the entire second pull.

violations.observation: The declared return-lever press is not visible in the consecutive contact window: Bot remains left of the house with an open gesture, then exits while the mechanism begins.
violations.smallest_correction: Place the left hand directly on the exposed lever for frames 608–614, show a small lever compression, then release before Bot exits.

violations.observation: At the wide archive display, two large blank yellow rectangles overlap the central house and command more attention than the live state; the intended three-state hierarchy becomes a wall of generic panels.
violations.smallest_correction: Move the bays fully outside the house silhouette and reduce their blank card area while retaining large roof and floor tokens.

violations.observation: Without captions, the tiny roof icons and thin floor bars do not clearly distinguish checkpoint-dry from failed-wet states; the panels read primarily as yellow rectangles.
violations.smallest_correction: Increase the pitched/flat roof tokens and level/sagging floor bars substantially, with stronger cream-versus-teal contrast, while keeping the live house unobscured.

sampling_limits: No MP4 playback or audio listening was performed. Findings use the supplied ordered decoded native frames, all consecutive temporal-window frames in manifest order, sparse shot samples and pixel-change traces. Pixel deltas were used only to locate holds/activity, not to infer semantic motion. Starts, stops and releases without dedicated consecutive windows cannot establish uninterrupted attachment beyond what adjacent supplied frames show.
